title: Gauhati High Court (division bench of Justices Kalyan Rai Surana and Susmita Phukan Khaund, observation of 5 Nov 2026, Scroll; reported by LiveLaw 10 Nov 20:33 IST and Scroll 11 Nov) holds that a PAN card and an EPIC (voter ID) cannot be accepted as proof of Indian citizenship unless the records supplementing them are proved, because both are issued on self-application/self-declaration without formal inquiry by the Income Tax Department or the Election Commission; the court upheld a Foreigners Tribunal opinion declaring a woman (not named by idly) a foreigner who entered India after 25 March 1971, finding she had not proved her link to her claimed father and grandparents or the family's continuous residence in Assam (Section 6A(2), Citizenship Act); 1966/1970 voter lists and a ration card did not establish the link and the original NRC acknowledgement was not produced (LiveLaw, Scroll). The same court called the point 'well settled' in a July 2026 case (Pratidin Time, Hub Network; also Taxscan, LawStreet).
